messages:
global-retail: Hi Redwood team — since yesterday's quant profile change (FP8 experimental) our product classification API is returning weird labels. Previously stable mapping, now class 'Returns' turns into 'Promotions' for a subset of inputs. No API errors; latency same. Affected model: redwood-alpha-1-fp8-canary, region eu-west-1, traffic ~1.8%. Example input and outputs attached. Please advise.

Jules (CS): Sorry you're seeing this—thanks for the example. Are you on Hosted? Can you include the request_id and a minimal curl/SDK repro? Also confirm whether you used any per-route overrides.

global-retail: Hosted. Sample request: request_id req_20260312_ba77c. Minimal repro: 
```
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer $API_KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"model":"redwood-alpha-1-fp8-canary","input":"Customer wrote: \"I want to return this item\". Best label?","max_tokens":32}'
```
Observed output (canary): "Promotions". Baseline (fp16): "Returns". Attached CSV with 12 cases showing semantic flips.

Anita (ML Eng): Thanks. FP8 rollout id QP-2026-03-12-EXP targeted eu-west-1 canaries. We'll take this seriously. Ravi — can runtime telemetry correlate request_id?

Ravi (Runtime): Pulled logs for req_20260312_ba77c. Runtime emitted a runtime-warning: `FP8_NUMERIC_UNDERFLOW attention_kernel.cpp:198 unscaled_exponent=-24`. Also got a downstream postprocess confidence bump for 'Promotions' driven by softmax skew. Repro locally with fp8 kernel when input tokens include long prefix (~600 tokens) + batch_size=3. Steps to repro locally: 
```
# launch local canary runtime image
docker run --rm -e REDWOOD_FP8=1 redwood/runtime:canary-20260312 
# client: batch of 3 requests with long prefix
python tools/send_batch.py --model redwood-alpha-1-fp8-canary --batch 3 --prefix-file long_conversation.txt
```
On repro you see `FP8_NUMERIC_UNDERFLOW` followed by changes in top-3 token probs. Hypothesis: FP8 quant mantissa/exponent handling underflows for attention accumulators when prefix token counts push exponent down; leads to small but systematic bias shifts.

deploy-bot: rollout QP-2026-03-12-EXP reached 45% in eu-west-1 at 2026-03-12T01:12:04Z.

Tom (Support): Two customer-safe mitigations: 1) Set per-route override to use `force_fp16_kernels` for redwood-alpha-1 models; 2) Temporarily pin model to `redwood-alpha-1-fp16-stable`. Suggest offering rollback for eu-west-1. Which should we execute?

Jules (CS): Customer requests immediate mitigation; prefer a regional rollback of canary FP8 profile for eu-west-1 and we'll offer credits if they want. Also ask them to try per-route override if they want zero change window.

global-retail: Please roll back — we'll validate. Also curious about root cause and timeline for fix.

Anita (ML Eng): Engineering plan: revert the FP8 canary in eu-west-1 now; open hotfix to clamp FP8 exponent ranges and add a denorm-to-zero guard in attention accumulators (PR #4750). We'll run eval suite on regression buckets after patch. ETA: rollback immediate; hotfix validation ~3h; full rollout of patched FP8 earliest 24h after validation.

Ravi (Runtime): Executed rollback for QP-2026-03-12-EXP in eu-west-1 at 2026-03-12T01:26:18Z. Confirmed canary instances draining and replaced with previous fp16/int8-compatible image. Monitoring for any perf delta.

deploy-bot: rollback QP-2026-03-12-EXP triggered by ops at 2026-03-12T01:26:20Z.

Tom (Support): For CS playbook — steps to propose to customers: 
- Ask them to re-run failing cases and confirm outputs stable after rollback.
- If they still observe flips, enable `force_fp16_kernels` per-route and collect failing request_ids.
- Request example set and we will run them through eval harness; include request_ids, timestamps, and any attached prompt noise.

Jules (CS): Messaging to send (draft): "Thanks for reporting. We've rolled back the experimental FP8 canary in eu-west-1 due to numerical instabilities that caused small probability shifts and label flips for a narrow set of inputs. You should see behavior return to baseline now. We'll follow up with a deeper postmortem and timeline for a safe FP8 re-release. Apologies for the disruption; we can offer account credit for the impacted window."

global-retail: Confirmed — initial checks show labels back to baseline. We'll exercise our 12-case suite and report if anything else pops. Appreciate the quick action.

Anita (ML Eng): Next steps for us: add regression tests that include long-prefix + batch workloads to the FP8 CI gate, add automated checks for softmax top-k shifts > threshold, and include exponent clamp in reference kernel. Owners: Anita + Ravi.

Ravi (Runtime): For runtime telemetry team: capture counters `fp8_underflow_count` and `attention_exponent_min` in canaries going forward, and alert if underflow_count > 0. We'll add to the dashboard.

Jules (CS): I'll close after postmortem is published. Please cc me on the writeup so I can share with the customer. Thanks everyone for the quick turnaround.

global-retail: Thanks, team — will wait for the postmortem.

Anita (ML Eng): Filing internal postmortem and will include repro scripts, telemetry traces, PR link (#4750), and the schedule for re-validation. Closing thread once postmortem posted. :pray:
